svg.title: Canonical Entity Modelling: Schema Evolution, SCD Type, and Delta Mutation Path
svg.desc: An original decision and internals diagram covering three silver-layer modelling decisions. First, a schema-evolution question: an incoming bronze column change is additive and merges automatically via Delta mergeSchema, unless a foreign key constraint exists on the target table, which freezes all further schema evolution until removed. Second, a historization question: does any consumer need to reconstruct a row's state as of a past date; a yes routes to SCD Type 2 with an internals cutaway showing the close-old/open-new MERGE mechanics and a warning about non-deterministic latest-row ordering, while a no routes to SCD Type 1 in-place overwrite. Third, a Delta mutation-path question for the SCD Type 2 write itself: whether to use classic copy-on-write MERGE or enable deletion vectors, shown as an internals cutaway of the merge-on-read soft-delete-plus-small-file mechanism with its measured before/after-OPTIMIZE performance trade-off and Delta protocol version increase. A closing node shows the V-Order and OPTIMIZE physical-layout decision that every path still converges on, with its measured write-time cost.
svg.text: Canonical entity modelling — schema evolution, SCD type, and Delta mutation path
Three silver-layer decisions plus the internals of the SCD merge and the V-Order/OPTIMIZE step every path shares
DECISION 1 · SCHEMA EVOLUTION AT THE SILVER MERGE TARGET

g.aria-label: Is the incoming bronze schema change additive?
g.title: Is the incoming bronze schema change additive? — Root question: new column, or a breaking change to an existing one?
mergeSchema applies additive changes automatically — Delta Lake supports schema evolution on MERGE/write via mergeSchema for new columns.

g.aria-label: Trap: foreign key constraint freezes schema evolution
g.title: Trap: a foreign key constraint freezes schema evolution — Adding an FK constraint between endpoint tables silently stops future Delta schema changes from syncing.
g.text: Adding a foreign key between endpoint tables freezes further
schema changes on those tables — later Delta schema evolution
(e.g. new columns) silently stops syncing until it's addressed.
Symptom: looks like a stalled sync, not an error.

svg.text: DECISION 2 · HISTORIZATION — SCD TYPE 1 OR TYPE 2

g.aria-label: Does any consumer need the row as it was at a past date?
g.title: Does any consumer need the row as it was at a past date? — The historization question that routes SCD type choice.
g.text: e.g. price at time of sale,
If none: complexity with no customer

g.aria-label: SCD Type 2 internals: close old row, open new row
g.title: SCD Type 2 internals — the MERGE closes the current row and inserts a new current row, keyed by a deterministic ordering column.
g.text: Requires a deterministic ordering key — see the

g.title: SCD Type 1 in-place overwrite — no version history kept; Delta time travel remains as an unmodelled recovery safety net.
g.text: MERGE updates in place, no history row

g.aria-label: Trap: latest row resolved without a deterministic ordering key
g.title: Trap: "latest row" without a deterministic ordering key — resolving latest-per-key by arrival time silently corrupts SCD history on retry.
g.text: time instead of source commit time looks
correct — until a retry reorders rows and
each rerun can record a different "current" row

svg.text: DECISION 3 · DELTA MUTATION PATH FOR THE SCD WRITE

g.aria-label: How should the SCD Type 2 write mutate the Delta table?
g.title: How should the SCD Type 2 write mutate the Delta table? — Classic copy-on-write MERGE, or merge-on-read via deletion vectors?
g.text: Frequent row-level UPDATE/MERGE traffic on this
table changes which mutation path is cheaper.

g.title: Deletion vectors: merge-on-read internals — soft-delete via a small binary marker file, filtered at query time, instead of a full file rewrite.
g.text: UPDATE soft-deletes the old row via a new .bin
marker, writing only changed values to a small
Pair with periodic OPTIMIZE, or the read cost compounds

g.aria-label: V-Order and OPTIMIZE apply after any modelling path is chosen
g.title: V-Order and OPTIMIZE apply after any modelling path — Type 1, Type 2, copy-on-write, or deletion vectors all still need periodic compaction.
g.text: V-Order + OPTIMIZE — the shared physical-layout step
Every path above still needs periodic OPTIMIZE; the V-Order table property alone only affects future writes
